description:
An issue mutation takes 0.3 s on a 1,100-issue repository and 1.3–1.8 s on an adopter repository of 876 issues, while reads of the same data take 8–75 ms. Nearly all of that time goes to capturing and hashing repository state the mutation never reads. The lock is held throughout, so concurrent agents queue behind it.

## Background

A mutation builds its read set as a closed repository image. One `issue update` captures about seven times:
- three phases in a preflight session;
- three phases again in the attempt session;
- one read-set revalidation at apply.

Each capture reads every registry, including the whole event log, and every issue file. It also reads every document referenced by any issue: working-tree files and pinned Git revisions. `RepositoryImage::close` then recomputes the SHA-256 digest of every entry the capture boundary has just hashed. The plan hash serializes each written file's bytes as a JSON number array. For an event append, that is the whole event log.

The domain work is issue-local. Documents are consumed in only two places:
- a state transition evaluates graph rules against plan documents;
- whole-repository validation checks document references.

The preflight session answers two questions before the claims guard is taken: whether leases are enforced, and, for lifecycle transitions, what the precheck gates need.

Measured on a tmpfs clone of the adopter repository:
- 876 issues;
- 1469 unpinned document references totalling 116 MB;
- 42 pinned revisions;
- a 3 MB event log.

On it, a label update takes 1.8 s and a refused update (no lease) takes 0.3 s on the smaller repository, because the refusal comes after six captures.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Closing a repository image computes no content digest for an entry whose identity the capture boundary derived from its bytes.
- [hard] REQ-02: An issue mutation captures only the plan documents its transition rules read. Issue document references, working-tree or pinned, are captured only by operations that run whole-repository validation.
- [hard] REQ-03: A mutation attempt captures its full base once. Work done before the claims guard reads only what the lease decision needs, except where a lifecycle transition runs precheck gates outside the lock.
- [hard] REQ-04: The plan hash commits to each written file's bytes through their content digest instead of serializing the bytes. Distinct bytes still yield distinct plan hashes.

## Notes

The 100 ms label-update criterion moved to the redo-record mutation epic on 2026-09-19 with the owner's approval. After this issue's changes, a changing label update on the adopter-scale clone takes 110 ms and an idempotent one 69 ms, down from 1.8 s and 1.3 s. The remainder comes from the publication mechanism that epic replaces.

Changed files are still detected before publication: the apply-time revalidation covers the smaller read set. Replacing the whole-file event-log rewrite with a true append, and scoping transition read sets to the dependency neighbourhood, are out of scope. They are the next candidates if the target is missed or tightened.
title: Issue mutations capture and hash far more repository state than they read
